author: product-requirements-expert
title: Filter the veterinarian directory by specialty on both surfaces
summary: Both veterinarian-directory surfaces accept an optional specialty filter that narrows the list to veterinarians holding that specialty; the machine-readable surface is reinstated as a supported capability with this as its first requested one.
acceptance_criteria: Filtering either surface by a specialty some veterinarians hold presents only those veterinarians, and the machine-readable surface returns them with a success response
The specialty match is on the whole name and case-insensitive: a case-different name matches, and the start of a stored name that is not the whole name does not match
Filtering by a specialty no veterinarian holds returns the ordinary directory with an empty veterinarian list and a success response on both surfaces
A blank or whitespace-only filter is treated as no filter and returns the whole directory on both surfaces
With no filter, both surfaces present the whole directory as before
On the page-at-a-time surface, paging counts only the veterinarians the filter matches
The machine-readable veterinarian surface is a supported capability
non_goals: Free-text veterinarian search stays out of scope (NG-9, narrowed)
Filtering by any veterinarian attribute other than specialty
notes: NG-9 narrowed 2026-08-06 to allow filtering the directory by a displayed attribute. Fresh id minted; withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and superseded by REQ-VET-003, its id not reused (Superseded list and Open Questions updated). URL and query-parameter mechanism is deferred to system-design.md#contracts.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fits the vet feature package unchanged in shape: both existing VetController routes gain an optional specialty filter. The filter is applied in-application over the cached collection (findAll()), matching the whole Specialty name case-insensitively, then paged in the controller for the HTML surface. Reuses the owner-search blank-handling pattern (OwnerController.processFindForm: strip(), treat empty as no filter) and the existing per-controller pagination helper. Recorded in system-design.md#contracts (VetController row now Implements REQ-VET-003; a one-line filter rule added under 'Invariants the rows cannot carry') and in ADR 2026-08-06-in-application-specialty-filtering. The stale Known Defects row calling the /vets route 'pending removal / serves no requirement' has been removed — the route is now a supported surface serving REQ-VET-003.
integration_points: VetController.showVetList (/vets.html): add optional specialty @RequestParam; when non-blank, filter the cached collection and build the Page from the filtered list; add the specialty to the model so pagination links preserve it; when blank/absent, keep the current findAll(pageable) path exactly
VetController.showResourcesVetList (/vets): add optional specialty @RequestParam; when non-blank, filter the collection before wrapping in Vets; when blank/absent, behave exactly as today
vetList.html: pagination links currently hardcode /vets.html?page=N and would drop the filter — thread the specialty parameter through every page link so paging stays within the filtered set
Vet.getSpecialties() supplies the Specialty names to match against; the whole-name case-insensitive test is vet.getSpecialties().stream().anyMatch(s -> s.getName().equalsIgnoreCase(filter))

patterns.description: blank/whitespace filter handling to mirror: null-or-strip(), empty string means broadest result — reuse verbatim for the specialty parameter
existing per-controller pagination helper (page size 5) to reuse for paging the filtered list

risks.risk: A database-level ignore-case query (e.g. a derived findDistinctBySpecialties_NameIgnoreCase) would inherit the per-vendor collation divergence that already makes PostgreSQL owner search case-sensitive (Known Defects), silently breaking the case-insensitive acceptance criterion on PostgreSQL
risks.mitigation: Match in-application with equalsIgnoreCase over the cached collection — the ADR decision; leaves VetRepository unchanged

risks.risk: Pagination links dropping the specialty parameter would reset the filter on page change, breaking 'paging applies to the filtered set'
risks.mitigation: Add the specialty to the model and append it to every pagination link in vetList.html; test paging within a filtered result

risks.risk: Conflating the two empty outcomes — a blank filter must yield the whole directory, a named-but-unmatched specialty must yield an empty list, both HTTP 200
risks.mitigation: strip() first and branch on emptiness before filtering, exactly as owner search does; cover both cases with distinct tests (theVetListShouldReturnTheWholeDirectoryForABlankSpecialty vs theVetListShouldReturnAnEmptyListForASpecialtyNoVetHolds)

risks.risk: Adding a parameterized @Cacheable repository method would multiply cache keys under the single 'vets' cache (open question 5)
risks.mitigation: Reuse the existing findAll() cache; add no parameterized cached query

notes: prd-entry lists VetRepository.java as a file target, but the recommended in-application design leaves VetRepository unchanged (it is supporting context, not an edit target); the whole-directory reads reuse the existing REQ-VET-001 methods. If the implementer instead chooses the repository route, an ADR revision is required because it reintroduces the PostgreSQL case-sensitivity risk. Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records precede this dispatch — silent skip. The Known Defects intro's 'final row' reference still resolves to the MySQL duplicate-detection row after removing the machine-readable-route row.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The filtered JSON path streams `findAll()` and accumulates into the mutable `vets.getVetList()` via `forEach(vets.getVetList()::add)`. Using `forEach` with a side-effecting method reference on a stream is an anti-pattern; the idiomatic form is to collect first and then bulk-add. The original unfiltered path used `vets.getVetList().addAll(this.vetRepository.findAll())` which was clean — the refactor regressed it. The `filter(...).toList()` result should be passed to `addAll`, matching the checklist item 'no side effects in methods named as queries' and the general stream-pipeline idiom.
findings.fix: Replace the stream-forEach chain with: `List<Vet> filtered = this.vetRepository.findAll().stream().filter(vet -> specialtyFilter == null || holdsSpecialty(vet, specialtyFilter)).toList(); vets.getVetList().addAll(filtered);`

findings.description: The new `findPaginated` method (introduced by this change) accesses the field as unqualified `vetRepository` (lines 68, 73), while the pre-existing `showResourcesVetList` method uses `this.vetRepository` (line 86). Within the same class body, mixing qualified and unqualified field access creates a false signal — a reader may assume the difference is intentional. The inconsistency was introduced when `findPaginated` was added without matching the existing `this.` qualifier style.
findings.fix: Qualify field access in `findPaginated` to `this.vetRepository.findAll(pageable)` and `this.vetRepository.findAll()` to match the style used in the rest of the class.

findings.description: `pageable.getOffset()` returns `long`; the unchecked cast `(int) pageable.getOffset()` is a lossy narrowing conversion. For a vet directory with small `page` values this is safe in practice, but the silent truncation is invisible to a reader and will produce wrong `start` values if `page` is ever unexpectedly large. `Math.toIntExact()` throws `ArithmeticException` on overflow and makes the bound explicit; alternatively, keeping `start` as `long` and adjusting the arithmetic avoids the cast entirely.
findings.fix: Replace `int start = (int) pageable.getOffset();` with `int start = Math.toIntExact(pageable.getOffset());` to make the range assumption explicit and detectable.

approved_aspects: Format check (`./gradlew checkFormat`) passes cleanly — no formatting issues

Unfiltered path is genuinely preserved: `normalizeSpecialty(null)` returns null, `findPaginated` takes the `if (specialty == null)` early-return branch calling `vetRepository.findAll(pageable)`, matching the pre-change behavior exactly
`normalizeSpecialty` correctly mirrors the owner-search blank-handling pattern (`strip()`, empty-as-null) as mandated by the design
`holdsSpecialty` is a clean, well-named private static helper — the `equalsIgnoreCase` whole-name match is correct and vendor-independent
`PageImpl` construction from the filtered list is arithmetically correct; the `start >= filtered.size()` guard properly handles out-of-range page requests with `List.of()`

The HTML template threads `specialty=${specialty}` through all five pagination link variants (numbered pages, first, previous, next, last); Thymeleaf omits null parameters so the unfiltered case produces clean URLs without a dangling `specialty=` parameter

Test method names follow BDD conventions and cover the full acceptance-criteria matrix: single match, case-insensitive match, prefix non-match, unmatched specialty, blank filter, absent filter, and paging within filtered set

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Reflected XSS not exploitable: user-controlled `specialty` reaches vetList.html only via Thymeleaf `@{...(specialty=${specialty})}` link expressions, which URL-encode the query-parameter value and HTML-escape the th:href attribute output; the change also replaced the prior unsafe string-concatenation URL form (@{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'}) with the safe parameterized form

No injection surface: specialty is matched with equalsIgnoreCase over the in-memory cached collection, so no SQL/JPQL/derived query is built from the input; no command exec, path traversal, or deserialization introduced

Input normalization is null/whitespace-safe (normalizeSpecialty strips and coerces blank to null); specialty is never reflected as text (no th:utext, no text output) on either the HTML or JSON surface
No new data exposure: the JSON /vets surface returns a filtered subset of the same collection already served, no additional fields or endpoints
Supply chain unchanged: no build.gradle/pom.xml or dependency changes in the change set; Spring Boot 4.1.0 baseline untouched
Resource-consumption angle bounded and documented: in-memory filter runs over the small cached vet collection per ADR 2026-08-06; no attacker-amplifiable expansion introduced

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Three expectations in `theVetListShouldPageWithinTheFilteredSpecialty` are bare literals not derived from the test setup: `6L` (totalItems), `2` (totalPages), and `hasSize(1)` (page-2 content). A reader must count the loop iterations (10..15 = 6) and mentally divide by the controller's hardcoded page size (5) to verify them. This violates the Derived Expectations rule in testing-principles.md (§ Derived Expectations): "If an expected value is a function of the inputs, express that function explicitly."
findings.fix: After building the surgeons list, derive expectations from it: `long total = surgeons.size();` (6L), `int pageSize = 5;` (matches the controller constant), `int page2Size = (int)(total % pageSize);` (1), `int pages = (int)Math.ceil((double)total / pageSize);` (2). Replace the bare literals with these named values so the arithmetic is visible in the test.

findings.description: The PRD acceptance criterion reads 'given a blank or whitespace-only filter' as a single combined case, and testing-principles.md (§ Edge Case Coverage) requires all documented edge cases to have dedicated test cases. The whitespace-only case (`"   "`) is tested on both surfaces but the empty-string case (`?specialty=`) is not. In Spring MVC an absent parameter binds as null while `?specialty=` binds as the empty string `""`; `normalizeSpecialty("")` follows a distinct strip-then-isEmpty path from `normalizeSpecialty("   ")`. Both collapse to the same null return, but the PRD names them as a joint case and a dedicated test for `""` makes the contract explicit and guards against a regression in `normalizeSpecialty` that could treat an empty string differently from whitespace.
findings.fix: Add one test per surface that sends `?specialty=` (empty string) and asserts the whole directory is returned: for the HTML surface `.param("specialty", "")` expecting `hasSize(2)`; for the JSON surface the same with `.accept(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)`. Name them `theVetListShouldTreatAnEmptySpecialtyAsNoFilter` and `theVetsJsonShouldTreatAnEmptySpecialtyAsNoFilter`.
